title: David Sent Home Before the Battle
overview: As the Philistines prepare to fight Israel, their leaders refuse to let David, who has been living among them, march into battle with them, and he is sent home.

parts.label: Two armies gather (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The Philistines mass their troops at Aphek while Israel camps in the valley of Jezreel, setting up the battle where Saul will die. David, who had fled Saul and was living under the protection of Achish, a Philistine king, marches at the rear as part of Achish's personal guard, trapped between betraying his host and fighting his own people.

parts.label: The commanders object (vv. 3-5)
parts.note: The other Philistine leaders want to know why Israelites are in their army, and they fear David will switch sides mid-battle and win back Saul's favor by killing Philistines. They remember the old victory song praising David for killing far more Philistines than Saul did.

parts.label: Achish gives in (vv. 6-7)
parts.note: Achish praises David's loyalty, even swearing by Israel's God, perhaps out of courtesy to David, but he cannot overrule the others. The Philistines were led by five rulers, so even a king like Achish needed their agreement.

parts.label: David protests and leaves (vv. 8-11)
parts.note: David insists he has done nothing wrong and wants to fight 'the enemies of my lord the king.' Many readers think he was putting on a show of loyalty, and some notice that 'my lord the king' could quietly mean Saul, though no one can be sure what David truly intended.

disagreement: Christians differ on how to judge David here: some see his time among the Philistines as a lapse of trust from which God rescued him, while others see shrewd survival in a dangerous situation with no clear right choice.
think: Have you ever been spared a hard choice by a decision someone else made, and did it feel more like relief, luck, or something else?
